questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in reported speech.

Sheena said, 'I am flying a kite.'

options.text: Sheena said that she had flown a kite
Sheena said that she has been flying a kite.
Sheena said that she was flying a kite.
Sheena says she was flying a kite.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Sheena said that she was flying a kite.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When converting from direct to reported speech, changes are made to pronouns, verb tense, and time expressions.
 
• The direct speech sentence is: "**Sheena said, 'I am flying a kite.'**"
 
• The pronoun "**I**" changes to "**she**" in reported speech.
 
• The present continuous tense "**am flying**" changes to the past continuous tense "**was flying**" in reported speech.
 
• The correct reported speech sentence is "**Sheena said that she was flying a kite.**"

Therefore, the correct answer is option 3.

Correct Sentence: *"Sheena said that she was flying a kite."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other options are incorrect for the following reasons:
 
• **Option 1: "Sheena said that she had flown a kite."**
 
 
• Reason: This option is incorrect as it changes the tense to past perfect, which is not appropriate here.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: "Sheena said that she has been flying a kite."**
 
 
• Reason: This option is incorrect as it keeps the present perfect continuous tense, which should change to past continuous.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: "Sheena says she was flying a kite."**
 
 
• Reason: This option is incorrect as it changes the reporting verb to the present tense "says" instead of maintaining the past tense "said."

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in passive voice.

The police is interrogating the peons of my school.

options.text: The peons of my school are being interrogated by the police.
The peons of my school has been being interrogated by the police.
The peons of my school have been being interrogated by the police.
The peons of my school were being interrogated by the police.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'The peons of my school are being interrogated by the police.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When converting a sentence from active voice to passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• The active sentence is: "**The police is interrogating the peons of my school.**"
 
• The object "**the peons of my school**" becomes the subject in the passive sentence.
 
• The verb tense used in the active sentence (present continuous) is changed to the corresponding passive form ("**are being interrogated**").
 
• The agent "**by the police**" is added at the end of the sentence.
 
• The correct passive sentence is: "**The peons of my school are being interrogated by the police.**"

Therefore, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct Sentence: *"The peons of my school are being interrogated by the police."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The other options are incorrect for the following reasons:
 
• **Option 2: "The peons of my school has been being interrogated by the police."**
 
 
• Reason: This option is incorrect because "has been being interrogated" is not grammatically correct for the subject "the peons" (which is plural).
 
 
 
• **Option 3: "The peons of my school have been being interrogated by the police."**
 
 
• Reason: This option is incorrect because "have been being interrogated" is not a standard construction for present continuous tense in passive voice.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: "The peons of my school were being interrogated by the police."**
 
 
• Reason: This option is incorrect as it changes the tense from present continuous to past continuous.

questions.question: What is played in a Dhamaal song after blowing into a conch shell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Musindo**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• After blowing into a conch shell in a Dhamaal song, the musindo, an East African percussion instrument, is played.
 
• The slow playing of the musindo and the ritual foot thumping marks the onset of the singing and dancing Dhamaals.
 
• The Siddis of Gujarat incorporate these instruments as part of their spiritual musical traditions.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Table** - This term does not relate to the musical instruments mentioned in the passage.

questions.question: Select the most suitable word from the passage which means ‘excited’.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Frenzied**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"excited"** means feeling or showing happiness and enthusiasm (उत्साहित).

 
 
• **Example: **The children were **excited **about their upcoming field trip.
 
 
 
• **"Frenzied" **refers to a state of intense, often chaotic activity, resembling or involving frenzy (उत्साहित / पागलपन भरा).
 
 
• **Example: **The crowd broke into a **frenzied **dance as soon as the band began to play.
 
 
 
• Since "**frenzied**" implies a high level of excitement and activity, it is the most suitable word in the given context.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Spiritual **(आध्यात्मिक): Relating to or affecting the human spirit or soul as opposed to material or physical things.

 
 
• **Example:** He went on a **spiritual **journey to find inner peace.
 
 
 
• **Ritual **(अनुष्ठान): A religious or solemn ceremony consisting of a series of actions performed according to a prescribed order.
 
 
• **Example: **The annual **ritual **of lighting lamps is observed with great devotion.
 
 
 
• **Percussion** (वाद्य यंत्र): Musical instruments played by being struck or scraped such as drums, cymbals, or xylophones.
